title: Japan's health ministry suspends drug supply system after unauthorized access reported by its operator
date_note: Operation of the system has been stopped since 17 November 2026 per the ministry's notice, published 18 November.
org: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (Japan)
geo_basis: agency headquarters in Tokyo; the notice names no other place
summary: Japan's health ministry says NTT Data, which operates its drug supply stability and distribution confirmation system, reported unauthorized access by a third party; operation has been stopped since 17 November 2026. The notice says some stored data was viewed, there is a trace of an attempt to rewrite it, and names and contact details of some company staff may have leaked. An uploaded unauthorized file was deleted. The cause and scope are under investigation.
plain: Japan's health ministry has stopped a system used to report and check drug supply after unauthorized access. Contact details of some drug company staff may have leaked; the cause is still being investigated.
exec: A national drug supply reporting system is offline; contact details of some company staff may have leaked, and the cause and scope are under investigation.
action: Medical professionals: use the supply-status Excel files on the ministry's website while the system is down; follow the ministry's notice for restart.
impact: System stopped; the notice gives no figures.

sources.name: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare

validation.note: Primary source: the ministry's own notice of 18 Nov 2026. A note.com blog (20 Nov) repeats it; not cited.
